story.title: Cameroon Separatist Leader Denies War Crimes Charges in Norway
story.summary: Lucas Cho Ayaba, a leader of the Cameroon separatist movement, pleaded not guilty in a Norwegian court to charges of being an accessory to war crimes and terrorism. He is accused of orchestrating attacks that resulted in civilian casualties.

timeline_highlights.title: Israeli Opposition Leader Condemns Attacks on Palestinian Villages as 'Jewish Terrorism'
timeline_highlights.summary: Israeli opposition leader Gadi Eisenkot has condemned a series of arson attacks on Palestinian villages in the occupied West Bank, labeling them as 'Jewish terrorism.' The attacks involved Israeli settlers setting fire to vehicles and properties in multiple locations. In response, Israeli authorities have initiated an investigation into the incidents.
key_facts: Arson attacks occurred in several Palestinian villages in the West Bank.
Gadi Eisenkot condemned the attacks as 'Jewish terrorism.'
Israeli authorities have opened an investigation into the incidents.

event_overview.title: About West Bank Violence
event_overview.subject: West Bank Violence
event_overview.summary: West Bank violence refers to recurring attacks, confrontations and other coercive incidents affecting Palestinians, Israeli settlers and Israeli forces across the West Bank, including damage to people, homes, farmland, livestock and essential infrastructure. The November 2026 developments concern alleged settler attacks on Palestinian communities within a wider pattern that UN humanitarian monitors document separately from other forms of violence in the territory.

facts.label: Location and context
facts.value: The West Bank, including East Jerusalem, is treated by the United Nations and the International Court of Justice as part of the Occupied Palestinian Territory; the ICJ’s July 19, 2024 advisory opinion addressed Israeli policies and practices there, including settlements and settler violence.

facts.label: Legal framework
facts.value: UN Security Council Resolution 2334, adopted in 2016, states that Israeli settlements in Palestinian territory occupied since 1967, including East Jerusalem, have no legal validity under international law. Israel disputes this characterization and maintains claims and security positions concerning the territory.

facts.label: How incidents are tracked
facts.value: OCHA has documented West Bank casualties since 2005 and settler violence since 2006, counting settler attacks that result in Palestinian casualties, property damage, or both.

facts.label: Recent pattern
facts.value: OCHA recorded more than 1,600 settler attacks causing Palestinian casualties and/or property damage from January through mid-September 2026, affecting 275 Palestinian communities; reported effects included injuries, arson and damage to homes, crops, water systems and other infrastructure.

facts.label: Displacement impact
facts.value: OCHA reported that settler attacks and related access restrictions displaced more than 6,500 Palestinians between January 2023 and August 2026, alongside damage to livelihoods and essential services.

event_overview.scope_note: This Muninn timeline follows the selected November 22, 2026 attacks and related Israeli political reaction; it does not attempt to catalogue all West Bank violence, settlement activity, military operations, legal claims or wider Israeli-Palestinian conflict developments.

related_stories.title: China Reveals Crew for Upcoming Space Mission Including Pakistani Astronaut
related_stories.summary: China has announced the crew for its upcoming Shenzhou-24 mission, which includes Muhammad Zeeshan Ali, a Pakistani astronaut. Ali will be the first foreigner to board China's Tiangong space station. The mission is set to launch on Wednesday.

related_stories.title: Jensen Huang Returns to Nvidia Amid Economic Focus
related_stories.summary: Jensen Huang has returned to his role as CEO of Nvidia, a move that President Trump claims will bolster the nation's economic growth through advancements in artificial intelligence. Trump's involvement in Huang's return highlights the administration's emphasis on AI as a key driver for economic development.
